figures.name: 00-roadmap
figures.title: Structure of the theoretical background
figures.description: Section 2.1 leads to two routes: established methods in Section 2.2, and the tensor route through Sections 2.3 to 2.6. Both routes meet in fair evaluation, Section 2.7, and the evidence review, Section 2.8.

figures.name: 01-time-series-tracks
figures.title: A multivariate time series
figures.description: Three invented tracks measured at the same 48 hours: temperature with one dot per hour, relative humidity, and wind speed. One temperature observation at hour 30 is highlighted.

figures.name: 02-trend-season-noise
figures.title: Trend, seasonality, and noise
figures.description: An invented hourly series over four days and its three additive ingredients: a rising trend, a daily seasonal cycle, and irregular noise.

figures.name: 03-memory-and-random-walk
figures.title: Memory and the random walk
figures.description: Left: the autocorrelation of an invented hourly temperature series is high for short lags and peaks again at 24 and 48 hours. Right: a random walk history with five equally likely continuations; the naive forecast repeats the last value.

figures.name: 04-origin-window-horizon
figures.title: Forecast origin, input window, and horizon
figures.description: An invented hourly series is known up to the forecast origin. The last 24 values form the input window. The next 24 hours form the horizon, where only a forecast exists.

figures.name: 05-chronological-split
figures.title: Chronological split and rolling origins
figures.description: A series is divided in time into training, validation, and test parts. In the test part, forecasts start from several successive origins.

figures.name: 06-recursive-and-direct
figures.title: Recursive and direct multi-step forecasts
figures.description: Recursive: a one-step model is applied three times and its own forecasts move into the input window. Direct: one model returns all three future values at once.

figures.name: 07-repeat-last-value
figures.title: Measured history and forecast
figures.description: The forecast repeats the last observed value and is therefore horizontal.

figures.name: 07-repeat-seasonal-pattern
figures.title: Measured history and forecast
figures.description: The forecast repeats the hourly observations from the previous day.

figures.name: 08-sliding-windows
figures.title: One training example from four historical measurements
figures.description: Four temperatures were measured at successive hours. The first three are grouped as input; the fourth is the observed target, not a predicted or calculated value.

figures.name: 08-learning-from-error
figures.title: Prediction error during training
figures.description: An illustrative model predicts 14 degrees from inputs 12, 13, and 15. The observed target is 16, so the prediction is two degrees too low. Training uses such errors across examples to adjust parameters.

figures.name: 09-under-and-overfitting
figures.title: Underfitting and overfitting
figures.description: Three models fitted to the same twelve invented points. The straight line misses the shape, the smooth curve follows it, and the flexible curve passes through every point but departs from the true curve between them.

figures.name: 10-linear-lag-model
figures.title: Linear lag regression as a weighted sum
figures.description: Four recent values are multiplied by learned weights, summed, and shifted by a bias. The most recent value has the largest weight. The result is the forecast for the next step.

figures.name: 11-trees-and-boosting
figures.title: Decision trees and gradient boosting
figures.description: A decision tree asks yes-or-no questions about temperature, hour, and wind and ends in leaves with predicted changes. Gradient boosting adds many small trees, each fitted to the remaining errors.

figures.name: 12-recurrent-memory
figures.title: A recurrent network with memory
figures.description: Five observations are read one after another by the same cell. A hidden state passes from step to step as a memory, and the last state produces the forecast of the next value.

figures.name: 13-patches-and-attention
figures.title: Patches and attention
figures.description: An invented series is cut into six daily patches. Each patch becomes a token. Arcs from the last token show attention weights; the strongest link goes to the previous day.

figures.name: 14-pretrained-zero-shot
figures.title: Zero-shot forecasting with a pretrained model
figures.description: Many small series of different shapes represent the pretraining collection. The pretrained model then receives the history of a new series and forecasts its continuation without further training.
